scope: B02 Green run, breakout analysis, Mode A invalidation and confirmed-reset race, lines 235–327 only
provenance: Separate same-assistant source-first pass. Group contracts derived directly from pinned source; category rows link coordinate and operation. Historical W1 interpretations retained separately. No embedded production implementation or runtime trace.

groups.interpretation: Bullish detector inherits DetectorBase. Green-run helper returns price and owning row; signature alone validates nothing.
Compute predecessor index FirstRed minus one before checking stage bounds.

First reject predecessor below selected start; only otherwise read predecessor tag, require exact GREEN. Either failure raises ValueError. No explicit upper-range check; native indexing errors propagate.

Initialize run_start at predecessor. While above start, test immediately preceding tag exactly GREEN; decrement once each success, stop on first failed boundary/tag. Does not search disjoint earlier run.
Delegate inclusive maximum_high(run_start,run_end); returns owner from base, no extra tie or price transform.
Breakout analysis accepts candidate and candle, does not locally require main High>BoxTop; selection authority is caller.
Evaluate comparison of top-source index to First; if strictly earlier use top source+1, otherwise top source itself; no clamp or selected-range validation.
Truthy intrabar_start wins; otherwise lookup derived main timestamp. Source-index calculation precedes this truthiness decision.
End is supplied Break candle timestamp plus inferred timeframe, not next main timestamp. Bisect both lower bounds independently, left inclusive/right exclusive; no local clamping of start to Break.
Ask lower index for first strict greater High than candidate BoxTop in bounds. Missing hit returns None without extrema or owner lookup.
Query min Low over [left,crossing+1), includes crossing row. No additional event filtering; input/index validity required.
Read timestamp at min position, then main_source_for_time; if no selected owner return None despite crossing. Owner is min event's main row, not necessarily crossing row.
Construct IntrabarAnalysis from crossing lower row, minimum price and selected main source. No candidate mutation or confirmation append here.
Mode-A invalidation helper's name/comment do not enforce candidate.mode or create Reset. Caller admits Mode A.
Select anchor_value whenever not None, including zero; otherwise leg_boundary_value. No normalization.
If selected level None return False before accessing candle low.
If main Low>=level return False; equality is not invalidation. High not consulted on this path.
After strict main low breach, if main High<=BoxTop return True; equality not breakout; no lower search.
When both main thresholds strictly crossed, compute current main interval [open,open+timeframe) via two lower bounds; no intrabar_start restriction.
First strict lower Low<invalidation_level index queried before breakout. No new Reset or candidate mutation.
First strict lower High>BoxTop index queried second, regardless of first result.
Missing invalidation returns True exactly when breakout also missing; when breakout exists returns False.
Invalidation present and breakout missing returns True.
Both present: invalidation position<=breakout position wins, including same physical lower row. Equal timestamps at different positions are not necessarily tie.
Confirmed reset helper accepts nullable candidate and confirmed bottom. Does not locally check main Low or that confirmed bottom belongs to accepted ledger.
Short circuit candidate None before accessing High/top; return True if None or main High<=candidate top. Caller supplies reset context.
Otherwise compute current full main lower interval by nominal end and bisect_left at both ends.
Query first strict Low<confirmed bottom then High>candidate top; both queries before result arbitration, not selecting another candidate.
No reset hit returns True only if breakout also missing.
Reset hit and no breakout returns True.
Both present reset wins when position<=breakout; same-position priority, not timestamp equality across distinct lower positions. Returns Boolean only.
